evals.name: bug-hunt-interval-merge
evals.expected_output: Formalizes interval merge in Lean under ./tmp/, finds via counterexample search that a contained interval shrinks the merged end (e.g. [(1,10),(2,3)] -> [(1,3)]), reports REFUTED with concrete input, returns fixed Python using max(out[-1][1], hi), ideally with the fix verified in Lean.

evals.name: refactor-equivalence-pow2
evals.expected_output: Formalizes both as BitVec 32 / UInt32 functions in Lean under ./tmp/, uses bv_decide or exhaustive checking, and reports the divergence at v = 0 (loop gives 1, bit trick gives 0) and the behavior for v > 2^31 (bit trick wraps to 0, loop never terminates / p wraps and loops forever or exits depending on wrap - must analyze). Verdict REFUTED with concrete inputs, plus a statement of the domain on which they DO agree (e.g. 1 <= v <= 2^31).

evals.name: complexity-naive-fib-calls
evals.expected_output: Builds a cost-instrumented twin in Lean under ./tmp/ counting calls, discovers/verifies calls(n) = 2*fib(n+1) - 1, states verdict (PROVED or FINITE-CHECKED over a range), and answers the dispute: call count ~ 2*fib(n+1), so proportional to fib(n+1) not fib(n) - teammate roughly right about order of growth but off on the constant/index; for n=40 that's ~331 million calls.
